platform.name: CrisPRO
platform.full_name: CrisPRO — AI-Driven Oncology Trial Intelligence Platform
platform.tagline: Metastasis-interception AI — decoding the 8 steps of cancer spread
platform.mission: Identify the patient populations and biological conditions under which oncology trials succeed or fail — before they cost $300M.

core_system.name: Two-Layer Drug Failure Prediction System
core_system.description: CrisPRO evaluates every oncology program across two independent failure axes. A trial can fail at Layer 1 (wrong target), Layer 2 (wrong patients), or both. Most expensive failures are Layer 2 — the target is real, but the enrolled population cannot respond.

layer_1.name: Target Biology (Target-Lock Score)
layer_1.question: Is this gene a real driver of the cancer step being targeted?
layer_1.method: Multi-modal evidence synthesis: DepMap essentiality, in vivo CRISPR screens, patient expression data, mechanistic literature

layer_2.name: Patient Selection (Mechanism Fit)
layer_2.question: Are the right patients being enrolled? Are their genomic and molecular profiles matched to the trial's mechanism of action?
layer_2.method: CrisPRO PATH A formula: fit = clip((p·t) / ‖t‖₂, 0, 1) — normalized dot-product of patient vector p and trial vector t, clipped to [0,1]

failure_framework.name: 8D Failure Vector Framework
failure_framework.description: Every decoded trial is classified across 8 failure domains. The primary domain (highest weight) determines the root cause of failure. Secondary domains identify compounding factors.

domains.name: Biology
domains.description: Target is not a genuine driver in the enrolled cancer type or stage. Gene is expressed but not functionally essential.

domains.name: Selection
domains.description: Patient population too broad — responder subgroup exists but is diluted by non-responders. Biomarker gate missing or set at wrong threshold.

domains.name: Architecture
domains.description: Trial design cannot detect the signal — single-arm, wrong endpoint, insufficient power, or missing stratification variable.

domains.name: Timing
domains.description: Drug administered at wrong disease stage — too early (target not yet active) or too late (resistance already established).

domains.name: Combination
domains.description: Combination partner is antagonistic, redundant, or creates pharmacodynamic interference.

domains.name: Resistance
domains.description: Pre-existing or rapidly acquired resistance mechanism bypasses the targeted pathway.

domains.name: Translational
domains.description: Preclinical-to-clinical translation failure — archived tissue, expression heterogeneity, or species-specific biology.

domains.name: Systemic
domains.description: Safety signal, regulatory hold, or systemic toxicity terminates the program before efficacy can be assessed.

grounding_register.description: 38-row evidence classification register tracking every quantitative claim in the CrisPRO platform against its primary source. Each row carries a VERIFIED / PROVISIONAL / HYPOTHESIS label.

key_findings.title: CEACAM5 IHC ≥50% threshold is prognostic, not predictive
key_findings.description: CARMEN-LC03 (Phase III, N=389): PFS HR 1.14 (P=0.82) in CEACAM5 IHC ≥50% population. The threshold was set too low — ≥50% captures patients who express CEACAM5 but cannot respond to ADC therapy. CEACAM5 IHC is a marker of tumor identity, not drug sensitivity.
key_findings.source: Besse et al. IASLC 2024 WCLC; Sanofi press release 2023-12-21

key_findings.title: CEACAM5 IHC ≥80% shows directional OS benefit (post-hoc, underpowered)
key_findings.description: CARMEN-LC03 post-hoc: CEACAM5 ≥80% OS HR=0.71 (CI not published). CEACAM5 50–79% PFS HR=1.38 (numerically harmful). The ≥80% threshold is the candidate predictive gate — but this is exploratory, underpowered, and CI not published. Must be labeled as trend, not established.
key_findings.caveat: Post-hoc, underpowered, CI not published. Label as trend only.

key_findings.title: CEACAM5 IHC is not predictive at any threshold in CRC (PROCEADE-CRC-01)
key_findings.description: PROCEADE-CRC-01 (N=40, 3L+ mCRC): ORR 7.5% confirmed; CEACAM5 IHC Spearman rho = −0.14 (P=0.4) — no correlation between IHC expression and response. The IHC threshold failure pattern from NSCLC does not resolve in CRC.

key_findings.title: cCEA ≥100 as a liquid biopsy proxy for CEACAM5 IHC ≥80%
key_findings.description: Gazzah et al. (PMC12720031): cCEA ≥100 ORR 41.7% (10/24) vs 8.1% (3/37), P=0.003 in CEACAM5 high-expressing NSCLC. IHC ↔ cCEA Spearman ρ=0.43 (n=92). cCEA ↔ cCEACAM5 ρ=0.99 (n=87). cCEA ≥100 prevalence in HE patients: 40.3% (25/62). NOTE: All data from NSCLC — application to CRC is by inference.
key_findings.caveat: NSCLC data only. CRC application is by inference. Must be labeled on every slide.

key_findings.title: SGN-CEACAM5C EU clinical hold — VKG linker + Topo1i toxicity signal
key_findings.description: NCT06131840 (tusamitamab sonditecan, SGN-CEACAM5C): EU clinical hold in France, Spain, Sweden, Netherlands. Shared VKG linker + Topo1i chemistry with discontinued PF-08046044 (terminated for toxicity). No efficacy data published. Competitive risk for the CEACAM5 ADC field.

key_findings.title: CEACAM5 CRC prevalence: 98.7% any-positivity; MSS CRC has HIGHER expression than MSI-H
key_findings.description: Jansen et al. Cancers 2024 (DOI:10.3390/cancers16234052): 98.7% CEACAM5 any-positivity in colorectal adenocarcinomas (pan-tumor TMA). MMR deficiency → reduced CEA (P<0.0001) — MSS CRC has HIGHER CEACAM5 expression than MSI-H CRC. CRLM CEACAM5 positivity: 79% (Warmerdam et al. EJNMMI Res 2025).
key_findings.source: Jansen et al. Cancers 2024; Warmerdam et al. EJNMMI Res 2025

transfer_lessons: CEACAM5 IHC ≥80% is the candidate predictive threshold — ≥50% is insufficient
cCEA ≥100 ng/mL is a liquid biopsy proxy for IHC ≥80% (NSCLC data; CRC inference only)

programs.headline: 7-trial MSS CRC IO failure corpus — the definitive evidence base for why immunotherapy fails in MSS colorectal cancer and the 3 conditions under which it doesn't: non-liver-metastatic disease, pTMB ≥28, and immune-inflamed tumor microenvironment.
programs.indication_focus: 1L–refractory MSS/pMMR metastatic CRC across 7 trials spanning vaccine, CPI, MEKi+CPI, and combination IO strategies

three_conditions_for_io_benefit.evidence: CO.26 liver-met Pint=0.02; REGONIVO US 0/5 liver-met responders vs 22% NLM ORR; RIN NLM ORR ~40% vs liver-met ORR ~5%
three_conditions_for_io_benefit.clinical_implication: Liver metastasis is a mandatory stratification variable. Liver-metastatic patients should be analyzed separately or excluded from IO enrichment strategies.

three_conditions_for_io_benefit.evidence: CO.26 pTMB ≥28 OS HR=0.34 (90% CI 0.18–0.63, p=0.022) vs ITT OS HR=0.73. pTMB ↔ tissue TMB Spearman r=0.13 (P=0.20) — plasma TMB is not a proxy for tissue TMB.
three_conditions_for_io_benefit.clinical_implication: Prospective pTMB measurement at enrollment is the strongest available IO enrichment strategy in MSS CRC. Tissue TMB is not a substitute.

three_conditions_for_io_benefit.evidence: AtezoTRIBE Immunoscore-IC high subgroup PFS HR ~0.50 (exploratory); MEDITREME CD8-high + TGF-β-low subgroup better outcomes; GRANITE ctDNA-low subgroup HR 0.50 (exploratory)
three_conditions_for_io_benefit.clinical_implication: Immunoscore-IC, CD8+ TIL density, or ctDNA-low status are candidate prospective enrollment gates. None are validated in a randomized Phase III.

key_findings.title: Pharmacodynamic T-cell responses do not translate to clinical benefit in MSS CRC
key_findings.description: GVAX (ORR 0% despite confirmed T-cell responses) and QUILT-2.004 (HR 1.061 despite CEA-specific T cells generated) both demonstrate that peripheral immune activation does not equal intratumoral effector function in MSS CRC.
key_findings.source: Yarchoan et al. Cancer Med 2019; Redman et al. Oncologist 2022

key_findings.title: MEK inhibition does not convert MSS CRC to immunogenic (Phase III confirmed)
key_findings.description: IMblaze370 (Phase III, N=363): OS no significant difference across atezolizumab + cobimetinib vs atezolizumab vs regorafenib. MEK inhibition definitively fails to overcome MSS CRC immune exclusion.

key_findings.title: pTMB ≥28 is the strongest IO enrichment signal in MSS CRC from a randomized trial
key_findings.description: CO.26 pTMB ≥28 OS HR=0.34 (90% CI 0.18–0.63, p=0.022). pTMB median 15.3 mut/Mb (IQR 9.5–26.2). Tissue TMB ≥10 OS HR=0.71 (p=0.47) — NOT predictive. pTMB ↔ tissue TMB Spearman r=0.13 (P=0.20).
key_findings.source: Loree et al. Clin Cancer Res 2024 (PMID 38727700); Chen et al. JAMA Oncol 2020

key_findings.title: Liver metastasis abolishes IO benefit — Pint=0.02 in randomized data
key_findings.description: CO.26: liver-met PFS HR=1.39 (90% CI 1.02–1.90) vs no-LM PFS HR=0.54 (90% CI 0.35–0.96); Pint=0.02. REGONIVO US: 0/5 liver-met responders vs 22% NLM ORR (5/23). RIN: NLM ORR ~40% vs liver-met ORR ~5%.
key_findings.source: Chen et al. JAMA Oncol 2020 (PMC10698621); Fakih et al. EClinicalMedicine 2023

what_we_offer.name: Trial Failure Decode
what_we_offer.tagline: Understand why a trial failed — before you repeat the mistake.
what_we_offer.description: CrisPRO applies the 8D failure vector framework to any completed or ongoing oncology trial. We identify the primary failure domain (Biology, Selection, Architecture, Timing, Combination, Resistance, Translational, or Systemic), extract the responder subpopulation that existed within the failure, and produce a transfer lesson set for your program.
deliverables: 8D failure vector report with domain weights and primary/secondary classification
Responder subpopulation identification (biomarker gate, ORR, PFS HR)
Transfer lesson set for your program design
Competitive intelligence: which competitors are repeating the same mistake
what_we_offer.example: CARMEN-LC03 (CEACAM5 ADC, Phase III, N=389): D2 Selection failure — IHC ≥50% threshold too low; ≥80% subgroup shows directional benefit. Transfer lesson: set IHC ≥80% as the enrollment gate for next-generation CEACAM5 programs.

what_we_offer.name: Patient Selection Package
what_we_offer.tagline: Find the patients who will respond — before you enroll the ones who won't.
what_we_offer.description: CrisPRO builds a two-gate patient selection framework for any oncology program. Gate 1 identifies the target expression threshold (IHC, genomic, or liquid biopsy). Gate 2 identifies the IO permissiveness or pathway context required for response. The output is an ENRICH / CONSIDER / EXCLUDE stratification table ready for protocol integration.
deliverables: Two-gate patient selection framework (Gate 1: target expression; Gate 2: pathway context)
ENRICH / CONSIDER / EXCLUDE stratification table with biomarker thresholds
Population size estimate: how many patients qualify under each gate
Liquid biopsy proxy identification (e.g., cCEA ≥100 as proxy for CEACAM5 IHC ≥80%)
Protocol language for enrollment criteria
what_we_offer.example: SAR445953 (CEACAM5-Topo1 ADC): Gate 1 = CEACAM5 IHC ≥80% (28% of MSS mCRC patients); Gate 2 = IO permissiveness (pTMB ≥28 or Immunoscore-IC high). Estimated addressable population: ~3,700 patients/year in US MSS mCRC.

what_we_identified.title: The IHC Threshold Failure Pattern — CEACAM5
what_we_identified.description: CEACAM5 IHC ≥50% is prognostic, not predictive. The ≥80% threshold is the candidate predictive gate. This pattern — setting the IHC threshold too low — is the primary reason CARMEN-LC03 (Phase III, N=389) failed despite CEACAM5 being a genuine target. The same pattern is at risk of repeating in PROCEADE-CRC-01 (CRC, Phase I) where IHC is not predictive at any threshold tested.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: CARMEN-LC03: PFS HR 1.14 (P=0.82) at IHC ≥50%; CEACAM5 ≥80% OS HR=0.71 (post-hoc, underpowered). PROCEADE-CRC-01: IHC Spearman rho=−0.14 (P=0.4).
actionable_for: Any CEACAM5-targeted program in CRC or NSCLC

what_we_identified.title: Liver Metastasis Abolishes IO Benefit in MSS CRC — Pint=0.02
what_we_identified.description: Liver metastasis is the single most important stratification variable for IO trials in MSS CRC. CO.26 (randomized): liver-met PFS HR=1.39 vs no-LM PFS HR=0.54; Pint=0.02. REGONIVO US: 0/5 liver-met responders vs 22% NLM ORR. RIN: NLM ORR ~40% vs liver-met ORR ~5%. Every IO trial in MSS CRC that does not pre-specify liver metastasis as a stratification variable is at risk of diluting the NLM signal.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: CO.26 Pint=0.02; REGONIVO US 0/5 liver-met responders; RIN NLM ORR ~40% vs liver-met ~5%.

what_we_identified.title: pTMB ≥28 is the Strongest IO Enrichment Signal in MSS CRC from Randomized Data
what_we_identified.description: CO.26 pTMB ≥28 OS HR=0.34 (90% CI 0.18–0.63, p=0.022) — the strongest IO signal in MSS CRC from a randomized trial. Tissue TMB ≥10 OS HR=0.71 (p=0.47) — NOT predictive. pTMB ↔ tissue TMB Spearman r=0.13 (P=0.20) — plasma TMB is not a proxy for tissue TMB. pTMB median 15.3 mut/Mb (IQR 9.5–26.2).
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: pTMB ≥28 OS HR=0.34 (90% CI 0.18–0.63, p=0.022). CI NOTE: 90% CI 0.18–0.63 is the authoritative value (field standard for Phase II IO trials in MSS CRC). Published abstract also reports 95% CI 0.13–0.85.

what_we_identified.title: RS-High is the ATR Responder Gate — 8x ORR Difference
what_we_identified.description: Berzosertib (M6620) ORR 40% in RS-High vs 5% in RS-Low — an 8x difference. Responders existed within the failed ITT population. The trial failed because RS-High patients were not pre-selected. This is the canonical example of a D2 Selection failure where the target is real but the patient gate is missing.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: RS-High ORR 40% vs RS-Low ORR 5% (Yap et al. Cancer Discov 2020, NCT02595892).

what_we_identified.title: PTEN-Loss is the WEE1i Resistance Marker — ORR 0% vs 23%
what_we_identified.description: Adavosertib (AZD1775) ORR 0% in PTEN-loss vs 23% in PTEN-intact; PFS HR 1.82 (PTEN-loss) vs 0.55 (PTEN-intact). PTEN status is a mandatory exclusion criterion for WEE1i programs. Including PTEN-loss patients in a WEE1i trial guarantees ITT dilution.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: PTEN-intact ORR 23% vs PTEN-loss ORR 0%; PFS HR 0.55 vs 1.82 (Lheureux et al. Clin Cancer Res 2021, NCT03579316).

what_we_identified.title: OV ZEB1 is a Bevacizumab-Arm Prognostic Marker — HR=2.500 at Median Split
what_we_identified.description: ZEB1 expression is a prognostic marker in the bevacizumab arm of ovarian cancer trials. Continuous Cox: HR=1.4803 (95% CI [1.1188, 1.9586], p=0.006042, c-stat=0.6444). Median split: HR=2.500 (95% CI [1.322, 4.727], log-rank p=0.0036, FDR=0.0499). Arm interaction: HR=1.243 (p=0.246) — PROGNOSTIC_NOT_ARM_SPECIFIC.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: HR=1.4803 (continuous Cox); HR=2.500 (median split, FDR=0.0499). Arm interaction p=0.246 — prognostic, not bevacizumab-specific.

what_we_identified.title: M2 Stratum Beneficial Median OS — 34.4 Months
what_we_identified.description: M2 stratum calibration: GEO 74.0% vs published 73.9% (within 0.1%). M2 stratum beneficial median OS: 34.4 months (95% CI 32.7–38.8), p=9.52×10⁻⁵. what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: M2 beneficial median OS 34.4 months (CI 32.7–38.8), p=9.52×10⁻⁵.

what_we_identified.title: cCEA ≥100 as Liquid Biopsy Proxy for CEACAM5 IHC ≥80%
what_we_identified.description: IHC ↔ cCEA Spearman ρ=0.43 (n=92). cCEA ↔ cCEACAM5 ρ=0.99 (n=87) — near-redundant. cCEA ≥100 ORR 41.7% (10/24) vs 8.1% (3/37), P=0.003 in CEACAM5 high-expressing NSCLC. cCEA ≥100 prevalence in HE patients: 40.3% (25/62). CAVEAT: All data from NSCLC (NCT02187848). Application to CRC is by inference only.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: cCEA ≥100 ORR 41.7% vs 8.1% (P=0.003); IHC ↔ cCEA ρ=0.43 (Gazzah et al. PMC12720031).
actionable_for: Any CEACAM5 program seeking liquid biopsy enrollment gate
what_we_identified.caveat: NSCLC data only. CRC application is by inference. Must be labeled on every slide.

what_we_identified.title: Pharmacodynamic Dissociation — T-Cell Responses ≠ Clinical Benefit in MSS CRC
what_we_identified.description: GVAX (ORR 0% despite confirmed T-cell responses in 100% of patients), QUILT-2.004 (HR 1.061 despite CEA-specific T cells generated), PolyPEPI1018 (T-cell responses in 100% of patients, no objective responses), PANVAC (T-cell responses >70%, no OS benefit). Peripheral immune activation does not equal intratumoral effector function in MSS CRC. This is the most important lesson for any vaccine program in this indication.
what_we_identified.quantitative_anchor: GVAX ORR 0% (n=22); QUILT-2.004 HR 1.061; PolyPEPI1018 100% T-cell response rate, 0% ORR.
actionable_for: Any vaccine program in MSS CRC

value_propositions.headline: We've decoded 42 trials across 7 programs.
value_propositions.body: From ATR/DDR inhibitors in ovarian cancer to CEACAM5 ADCs in NSCLC and CRC to whole-cell vaccines in MSS colorectal cancer — CrisPRO has built the most comprehensive oncology trial failure corpus in the field. value_propositions.headline: The patients who respond are hiding inside every failed trial.
value_propositions.body: Berzosertib failed ITT — but RS-High patients had 40% ORR. CARMEN-LC03 failed at IHC ≥50% — but IHC ≥80% showed directional OS benefit. CO.26 was marginal ITT — but pTMB ≥28 patients had OS HR=0.34. The signal exists. The gate is missing. CrisPRO finds the gate.

value_propositions.headline: Two layers. Every failure.
value_propositions.body: Layer 1: Is the target real? Layer 2: Are the right patients enrolled? Most expensive failures are Layer 2 — the target is genuine, but the enrolled population cannot respond. CrisPRO's two-layer system has been validated retrospectively on CEACAM5 (CARMEN-LC03), ATR (ceralasertib), and MSS CRC IO (CO.26).
